listingTitle: Avoid repeatedly concatenating growing Node.js buffers
title: Avoid repeatedly concatenating growing Node.js buffers
why: Assigning Buffer.concat back to one of its input buffers copies all accumulated bytes on every loop iteration and can produce quadratic work.
suggestion: Collect chunks and concatenate once after the loop, or write them directly to a stream or preallocated destination.
limitations: Only direct assignments whose Buffer.concat array contains the same destination identifier inside a recognized braced loop are reported.
Aliases of Buffer, property destinations, reassignment through helper functions, bounded loop counts, and total byte volume are not inferred.

Loop/function structure and declaration evidence use masked executable source; comment, string and regex literal text does not establish a collection or structural scope. Analysis remains lexical rather than type-resolved.
